data.title: bn-10j7z: CML action schemas and planned quantifier expansion (RFC 0003 corr. 4 part B)

data.body:
[HIGH] Validate nested binder domains during guarded overflow checks

`overflow_free_quant` calls `candidates` for each nested binder, but then checks only the final quantifier body. `candidates` accepts an interval whose `fits` flag is false (`lower.rs:2924-2929`, `lower.rs:2972-2993`). Therefore, arithmetic in a nested binder domain can overflow at an outer hull candidate that the source quantifier excludes, while the outer guarded expansion is accepted.

A concrete shape is `forall i in 0..x: forall j in 0..min(i * 9223372036854775807, 0): true`, with `x` in `0..=2`. At `x = 0` or `x = 1`, source semantics never evaluate the nested domain for `i = 2`. The lowered outer implication still evaluates its right side, and model-core implication is strict (`crates/continuum-model-core/src/expr.rs:452-455`). The generated nested guard then evaluates `2 * i64::MAX` and returns an overflow error. This adds an error absent from the CML model and violates the exactness rule in RFC 0003 lines 231-238.

Failure modes: accepted lowering can replace a valid invariant verdict with `EvalError::Overflow`; the same path affects `forall` and `exists` because both generated connectives are strict.
Edge cases: `min` or `max` can keep the interval hull small while an intermediate operation has `fits = false`, so output-size checks do not reliably fail closed. The differential corpus generates arithmetic in bodies, but its domain generator uses only leaves and misses nested-domain arithmetic.
Rollback: fail closed on nested domain overflow until domain expressions join the overflow proof. A narrow fix should traverse every binder domain under the current outer intervals and return `GuardedOverflow` when any integer subexpression does not fit.
Monitoring: count `cml.lower.guarded_overflow` refusals and add differential cases that compare nested domains under states which exclude the overflowing outer candidate.
Validation: add the example above as a regression. Assert lowering returns `GuardedOverflow`, or prove oracle and lowered evaluation agree at `x = 0`, `1`, and `2`. Run the full locked gate after repair.

data.reason: [HIGH] Nested quantifier-domain arithmetic is omitted from guarded overflow validation, so accepted lowering can add strict-evaluation overflow errors absent from CML semantics. See th-3rpr6z. The independent risk:critical human-approval gate remains required.

data.body: Fixed in 25b0161. The plan's integer is now its interval (Plan::I = Option<Iv>). Inside a guarded instance, int_expr refuses any integer node whose value or intermediate result may leave i64, with enclosing binders at their whole hull and parameters at their whole universe. It is one pass over the lowered shape: nested binder domains, nested guards, membership operands, and bodies all go through that function. The separate overflow_free walker is removed. The reproducer is now refused as cml.lower.guarded_overflow, with neighbours for membership guards, max(), action-schema guards, and relational postconditions. The generator now draws domains with arithmetic, min/max, i64-scale multipliers, and nested binders; the 600-formula oracle differential requires both errors and refusals to occur. It found a second hole, now fixed: a range that is empty in every state folded to a constant and dropped its overflowing bounds. Such a range now keeps one guarded candidate, so the bounds are still evaluated. Mutants: guard context never entered, nested guards/domains skipped, and empty-range fold always taken are each caught by the new tests and by the generated differential. Re-check of action schemas and relational posts: an instance is evaluated only at a tuple of the declared universes, and a relational candidate at a value of the variable's domain. The CML relation ranges over both, and guard clauses and postconditions are strict in both, so neither adds evaluation outside the CML meaning. A guarded quantifier inside them is covered by the same check (test cr_3aqchd_guarded_domains_in_actions_are_proved_too).

[RESOLVED] Re-review at 25b01613 verifies the repair. `int_expr::<Plan>` now checks each integer subtree while a guarded context is active. Nested domains and nested guards retain the outer guarded context. A universally empty range with unsafe bounds retains one guarded candidate. The original reproducer now fails closed with `cml.lower.guarded_overflow`.

data.reason: Verified at target 25b01613. The full guarded subtree now participates in interval overflow checks.

data.body:
[HIGH] Preserve strict left-operand evaluation for empty membership

`membership` returns constant `false` when the set has no members before it lowers `x`. CML membership is strict. The direct oracle evaluates `x` first at `tests/quantifiers.rs:92-100`, and RFC 0003 requires strict error preservation at lines 225 and 238. For `state { x: Nat where x <= 2 }` with invariant `x * 9223372036854775807 notin {}`, CML reports overflow at `x = 2`. The lowered path returns `false` at lines 2729-2730, then `NotIn` negates it at lines 2669-2672. The programmatic invariant is therefore `true` instead of a typed evaluation error. This violates typed inconclusiveness and can let evidence outrun source semantics.

Failure modes: an empty membership can hide arithmetic overflow in init, an action guard, or an invariant. `notin {}` can become silent success. In an action guard, the change can enable a transition where CML evaluation fails.
Edge cases: the defect affects empty set literals and empty configured constant sets. It also bypasses `GuardedOverflow` inside a guarded quantifier because `int_expr` never sees the left operand. Negation, equivalence, and strict Boolean wrappers preserve the wrong constant.
Rollback: refuse empty-set membership until the lowering preserves evaluation. A narrow exact fix can lower `x` first and emit an always-false `InRange` over `x`, such as bounds `1..0`, so model-core evaluates `x` once before returning false.
Monitoring: track evaluation-error parity in the oracle differential. Add empty-set cases to the generated membership corpus and retain a count of exercised source errors.
Validation: add literal-empty and configured-empty regressions for `in` and `notin`. Compare the CML oracle and lowered model at safe and overflowing states. Cover init, action guards, invariants, and an outer guarded quantifier. Run the full locked gate after repair.

data.reason: [HIGH] Empty-set membership drops strict evaluation of its left operand. `notin {}` can turn an arithmetic evaluation error into `true`, including in invariants and action guards. Preserve the evaluation or refuse the construct, then add oracle-parity regressions.

data.body: Fixed in 64674a6. Empty membership (literal {} or a constant bound to an empty set) now lowers as !(x == x): false, but x is evaluated and fails where it fails. x goes through int_expr, so the guarded-overflow proof covers it. Regression cr_3aqchd_empty_membership_keeps_the_evaluation_of_its_operand checks in/notin against {} and E. Oracle and lowering agree at safe and overflowing states in invariants (80 checks, 40 errors), in an action guard (is_enabled vs oracle at each x), and in init (an overflowing operand gives the evaluation error, a safe one gives 4 states). Under a guarded quantifier an overflowing operand is refused and a safe one agrees. The generator now draws {}, E, S, literal sets, and the constant sides true &&, || false, false =>, if true then. The fold-back mutant is caught by both the regression and the generated differential. Fold audit of lower.rs: (1) empty membership: FIXED. (2) Non-empty membership, literal or constant set: every member and x evaluated, OK. (3) x in a..b with literal bounds: constant() folds only literal +,-,* with checked ops; on overflow it gives None and falls to the runtime compare, OK. (4) and/or/=>/iff with a constant side: no folding, strict node, OK. (5) if-then-else, constant condition included: lowered as (c && a) || (!c && b), all three evaluated, OK. (6) min/max with equal sides: no folding, OK. (7) Empty quantifier domain as a constant: from {} (nothing to evaluate), an empty constant set, a static a>b with both bounds fitting i64, or an always-empty range with fitting bounds (non-fitting bounds keep one guarded candidate since 25b0161), OK. (8) Static range or set literal expanded without a guard, dedup of static members included: taken only when every bound or member is a point interval that fits, so none can fail, OK. (9) Bound constants, parameters, binders, and variants as literals: no subexpression, OK. (10) Empty clause list as true (conjoin, balanced with no items): nothing dropped, OK. (11) Relational candidate substitution: placeholders replaced by constants, nothing dropped, OK. (12) Refinement constants in domain_of: declarations, not evaluated expressions, OK. Outside lower.rs: an unused def argument or let value is not evaluated after elaboration substitutes it. That is CML's defined meaning (RFC 0003 model functions), and the oracle evaluates the same normalized AST.

data.reason: Re-review at 64674a6b verifies the repair. Empty membership now lowers the operand before the empty case and represents false as !(x == x), so strict evaluation and guarded-overflow checks are preserved.

data.body:
[HIGH] Bound flat binder recursion before lowering

quantifier recursively consumes the flat binder slice through instance and the call back to quantifier at lines 3235-3245. The first balanced depth check occurs only after that recursion returns. shallow checks the Expr tree depth, but one Quant node stores every binder in one flat Vec. The accepted flat_binders shape at tests/resource_bounds.rs:513-519 already demonstrates thousands of binders in one node. An untrusted formula with thousands of singleton binders has fanout one and shallow output, yet Plan recurses once per binder and can abort the process with stack overflow instead of returning a typed refusal.

Failure modes: init, invariant, or action-guard lowering can overflow the process stack and abort the verifier on untrusted CML.
Edge cases: singleton domains avoid fanout limits; one flat Quant avoids AST-depth limits; action schemas can repeat the path. Empty first domains return early, but singleton domains reach the full recursion.
Rollback: refuse multi-binder quantifiers, or cap binder-list width before the first recursive call.
Monitoring: record binder-list widths and typed depth refusals. Treat any lowering stack abort as a security failure.
Validation: lower 4,000 and 100,000 flat singleton binders in the small-stack harness. Require success through an iterative implementation or cml.lower.expression_too_deep before recursion. Cover init, invariant, and action guard.

[HIGH] Meter plan-time set copies before performing them

Configured membership clones the complete set before charging its copy work. In Plan mode, work at lines 2159-2165 adds the requested cost only to predicted and burns one actual fuel unit. begin_site checks predicted only after the complete clause or action plan returns at lines 2199-2205. One action can contain many references to a maximum-size configured set, so planning performs occurrences times 65,536 element copies before any work-limit refusal. Quantifier domains repeat the clone at lines 3125-3129. Static literal domains also allocate and sort planning vectors at lines 3105-3113 before site enforcement. This defeats INV-016 resource bounds on untrusted CML.

Failure modes: a bounded source and schema-valid configuration can consume extreme CPU and allocation bandwidth before cml.lower.work_limit_exceeded, causing denial of service.
Edge cases: many membership clauses in one action defer the check longest; nested expressions do the same inside one top_bool site; configured sets maximize repeated copy work; static set domains perform unmetered plan-time allocation and sorting.
Rollback: refuse configured-set membership and set-domain expansion until planning work is bounded, or impose a small cardinality cap before copying.
Monitoring: compare wall-clock and allocation counts with Usage.work for large-set plans. Alert when planning work exceeds charged fuel.
Validation: reuse a 65,536-member constant set thousands of times in one action and under a tight work limit. Require refusal before the first large clone. Add static-set sort cases and exact node/work boundaries.

[MEDIUM] Charge the implicit true guard for every action instance

An empty action guard is planned as size zero here. Each generated instance still calls conjoin at lines 1828-1840, and conjoin constructs BoolExpr::Const(true) without node or charge at lines 2243-2246. An empty-guard action schema can therefore retain one uncharged output node per instance, up to 4,096 actions. Usage.nodes and a caller-supplied Limits.nodes no longer bound the actual lowered output. Plan and charge the implicit true node, then add an exact-limit regression for empty-guard schemas.

[MEDIUM] Implement the claimed Boolean set-membership path

RFC 0003 defines Bool as a scalar at notes/plan/rfcs/0003-continuum-model-language.md:202 and claims membership for scalar set literals and constant sets at line 227. membership always sends the left operand through int_expr here, but int_like excludes Bool at lines 2395-2402. Thus true in {true} is refused as cml.lower.non_integer_value. Configured Set[Bool] also fails because typecheck accepts Boolean members, while set-code extraction at lines 844-870 stores only integers, elements, and variants. This is fail closed, but it contradicts the implemented normative surface. Encode Boolean members as 0 and 1, or narrow the RFC claim and governance evidence.

[MEDIUM] Make generated action labels injective for sort elements

Run-config sort elements may contain any printable ASCII byte at config.rs:516-518. value_text returns that raw text at lines 1583-1609, then this code joins parameter fields with comma and equals delimiters. Valid tuples p="x,q=y", q="z" and p="x", q="y,q=z" both become A(p=x,q=y,q=z). ModelBuilder then rejects the duplicate action, so a schema-valid configuration fails the promised one-action-per-tuple expansion in RFC 0003 line 229. Use an injective escaped or length-prefixed canonical spelling and include collision regressions in model identity tests.

[MEDIUM] Do not let interval folding erase invalid primed reads

interval treats Primed exactly like State without checking budget.post or the relational slot table. For a singleton variable domain, x prime .. x prime becomes a point interval. candidates then takes the static branch at lines 3070-3079 and never calls int_expr, which bypasses PrimedOutsidePostcondition. The public lower API therefore accepts a hand-built NormModel with a primed binder domain outside a relational postcondition and silently drops the invalid reads. Validate Primed before interval folding, and add singleton-domain regressions outside postconditions and for non-relational variables.

data.reason: BLOCK: two HIGH resource-safety defects remain. Flat binder lists recurse before any effective depth guard and can overflow the process stack. Plan-time set cloning and sorting can perform multiplicative unmetered work before begin_site checks predicted fuel. Four MEDIUM contract defects also remain: implicit true action guards are uncharged, Boolean set membership contradicts the implemented RFC surface, raw sort-element labels are non-injective, and interval folding can erase invalid primed reads in hand-built NormModel input. The risk:critical human-approval gate remains separate and unsatisfied.

data.body: Fixed in f2e30c1. quantifier counts binders entered (budget.binder_depth) and refuses with cml.lower.expression_too_deep before entering binder number MAX_BINDER_NESTING + 1 (= MAX_EXPR_DEPTH + 1), before recursing. It counts depth, not scope-table size, so a hand-built model whose binders all share one number cannot evade the bound (found in adversarial pre-review). A repeated number now shadows and restores lexically, fixing a spurious refusal of q(q(..)) for an inlined def. Tests: flat_binder_lists_are_bounded_before_recursion covers 4,000 and 100,000 flat singleton binders in init, an invariant, and an action guard, in the small-stack harness under the memory limit (elaborated under a wide budget, since 100,000 binders exceed the default); 32 lowers and 33 is refused at each site. repeated_binder_numbers_do_not_evade_the_binder_bound covers 100,000 binders all numbered 0. Mutants (bound off; bound by table size) are caught.

Fixed in f2e30c1. Configured sets are Rc<[i64]>: membership and quantifier domains take a reference count, never a copy. In the plan, the predicted work is checked against the fuel left at every predicting step (predicted_fits), so a plan stops at the first step that decides the refusal, not after the site. A static set literal's sort is spent (effort) before it runs, in the plan as in the build, and predicted for the build. Constant lookups (ints, bools, sets) are now charged before the lookup, not after a contains_key guard. Test a_large_shared_set_is_refused_before_it_is_expanded: a 65,536-member set used 3,000 times in one action, under a limit of the bindings' work + 100,000, is refused WorkLimitExceeded, having spent fewer than 65,536 units past the bindings. Mutant (early prediction check off) caught.

Fixed in f2e30c1. conjoin of no clauses builds a charged true node. plan_action plans it as size 1 (and one unit of work), so the build draws it from the plan's prepaid output. Test the_implicit_true_guard_is_charged: a 16-instance schema with no guard equals the same schema with require true, in Model and in Usage.nodes, and the exact node limit holds (one node less is OutputTooLarge). Restoring the original (plan size 0, uncharged node) is caught.

Implemented in f2e30c1. For a Boolean x, x in S lowers to the balanced disjunction of x <=> m over literal members, and of x or !x over the codes of a configured Set[Bool] (bindings now store Bool members as 0/1). The empty set is x && !x (false, x evaluated). Hand-written corpus: (x == 0) in {true}, (x > 1) notin {true, false}, (y < 0) in B, (x == y) notin {}, forall b: b in B || b notin B, (x < 2) in {x == 1, y == 0}. All agree with the oracle on every state. RFC Scalars paragraph updated.

Fixed in f2e30c1. A sort element's bytes \\ , = ( ) [ ] are escaped with a preceding backslash in instance labels (escape_label). Enum variants, Booleans and integers need none. The width preflight uses the escaped length (escaped_len), charged by bytes. Test cr_3aqchd_instance_labels_are_injective uses elements [x,q=y  z  x  y,q=z  a\\b  (c)] with A(p: Node, q: Node): 36 distinct actions, including A(p=x\\,q\\=y,q=z) and A(p=x,q=y\\,q\\=z). The unescaped mutant is caught. RFC Action schemas paragraph updated.

Fixed in f2e30c1. interval() gives a Primed node an interval only when budget.post holds and the variable is a relational slot. Otherwise it returns None, so candidates falls through to int_expr, which refuses PrimedOutsidePostcondition. Test cr_3aqchd_a_primed_domain_is_never_folded_away uses hand-built models (singleton domain x: Nat where x <= 0): a primed binder domain in an invariant, in an action guard, and in a postcondition of a kept, non-relational variable. Each is refused. Mutant caught. Also from the pre-review: a refinement clause's depth is now checked before domain_of and constant recurse over a hand-built model.

[MEDIUM] The repair is incomplete for relational actions. `crates/continuum-cml-elab/src/lower.rs:1905-1908` still derives `guard_size` as zero when the clause list is empty, then passes it at line 1926. `relational_action` uses that zero at lines 1342-1355 to charge every candidate copy, although `subst_bool` copies the generated `BoolExpr::Const(true)` at line 1366. The earlier aggregate check overestimates this path, so it fails closed, but `Usage.nodes` under-reports the persisted model by one guard node per candidate and measured exact limits cannot replay. Pass the actual conjoined measure (`1` for an empty guard), and add an empty-guard relational exact-limit regression.

[MEDIUM] Include the implicit true node in empty-init evaluation work. `crates/continuum-cml-elab/src/lower.rs:1178-1181` computes `predicate_size = 0` for `init {}`, while `conjoin` now creates and charges a `BoolExpr::Const(true)` here. `init_work` therefore omits one evaluation step for every enumerated state. An empty init can admit up to `MAX_INIT_BINDINGS + 1` candidates before refusal, so untrusted input performs that work outside `Limits.work` and `Usage.work`. Use the actual conjoined size (`1` for empty) and add exact-work and wide-domain empty-init regressions.

data.reason: Verified at f2e30c1: configured sets use shared Rc slices, predictions fail as they grow, and static sorts spend fuel before sorting.
Verified at f2e30c1: sort values escape every label delimiter and backslash; width uses the escaped byte length.
Verified at f2e30c1: Boolean literal and configured-set membership lower through Boolean expressions, including strict empty membership.
Verified at f2e30c1: Primed receives an interval only in a relational postcondition; invalid reads fall through to the typed refusal.
Verified at f2e30c1: binder depth is checked before recursion and repeated binder numbers shadow and restore lexically.

data.body: [MEDIUM] Charge the final membership operand copy, or move the original. In integer membership, `crates/continuum-cml-elab/src/lower.rs:2855-2858` calls `first.0.clone()` for the last member without `copy`; Boolean membership repeats this at lines 2894-2897. For a boxed expression tree this performs a full recursive allocation and traversal, but neither `work::<Build>` nor the plan prediction includes it. A one-member set triggers the unmetered clone every time, and quantifier or action-schema expansion multiplies it. The output precharge bounds retained size, but `Limits.work` and `Usage.work` no longer bound actual lowering work as the RFC claims. Move the original into the final comparison, or charge the clone, and add an exact-work regression with a large operand under fan-out.

data.reason: Three MEDIUM resource-accounting findings remain: empty relational guards under-report candidate output nodes, empty init omits true-predicate evaluation work, and membership performs an unmetered final operand clone.

data.body: Fixed in 70ffccc. conjoined_size gives 1 for no clause (the true that conjoin builds), else clause count plus sizes. relational_action now receives it, and so does the aggregate template check, which previously over-estimated with guard.size + 1 and failed exact limits. Test an_empty_relational_guard_is_charged_per_candidate: a hand-built relational action with no clause (1,000 candidates) is charged at least successor_work(1000, 2, 8), and it lowers at the measured limits while one node or one unit less is refused. Mutant (no max(1)) caught.

Fixed in 70ffccc. init_work now takes conjoined_size (1 for an init with no clause), so the evaluation of true per enumerated state is precharged. Test an_empty_init_is_charged_per_enumerated_state (hand-built empty init, 2^16 states): work is at least init_work(2^16, 1, 16), the exact work boundary holds, and a limit of the precharge alone is refused before any state is enumerated. Mutant caught.

Fixed in 70ffccc. The last comparison takes the operand itself, moved (take_or_copy, in the integer and Boolean paths), and every other use is a charged copy, so no clone of the operand remains. Test membership_operand_copies_are_charged: a 64- and 128-leaf operand, 4 members, 100 instances. Work covers the 3 charged copies per instance, grows linearly, and the exact work boundary holds. Crate audit of .clone() (this bone's code): lower.rs has 17; the other 136+13+9 in elab/types/config are pre-existing and covered by the inventory. In lower.rs: enum_tables (511/513/516) charged before; sort names and keys (796/817) charged before; the ConfigRefusal name (835, 679) is error-path text of at most 128 bytes; binding keys (895-897) charged before; relational update copies (1366) charged per candidate as copied; subst leaves (1400/1402/1422) are constants or variable names of at most 128 bytes, inside the precharged template; the param scope key (1724) is charged; the instance label and param key (1880/1885) are at most 128 bytes and in the planned name text; copy() (2716) charges first. Zero sizes from empty lists: conjoined_size (fixed; used by init and relational); plan_action's empty guard is 1; balanced over no items builds a charged node; the relational copied sum is 0 only for no updates, which copy nothing; the quantifier count 0 builds a charged constant; the membership n = 0 path is charged. No other size is derived from an empty list.

[RESOLVED] Re-review at 70ffcccd verifies the relational repair. lower.rs:2346-2350 assigns one node to an empty conjunction, lower.rs:1908 passes that measure, and lower.rs:1855-1868 uses the same value in the aggregate candidate check.

data.reason: Verified at 70ffcccd: empty relational guards are measured and charged as one node.

data.body: [RESOLVED] Re-review at 70ffcccd verifies the init repair. lower.rs:1173-1181 derives predicate_size through conjoined_size, whose empty case is one at lower.rs:2346-2350, before init_work charges every candidate.

data.reason: Verified at 70ffcccd: empty init predicates charge their true node per candidate.

data.body: [RESOLVED] Re-review at 70ffcccd verifies the copy repair. lower.rs:2697-2714 moves the final operand, and both integer and Boolean membership use take_or_copy at lower.rs:2888-2890 and 2923-2926. Only earlier uses call the charged copy path.

data.reason: Verified at 70ffcccd: the final membership operand is moved, not cloned.

data.body:
[MEDIUM] Charge each expanded ActionDecl in the output plan

The non-relational schema plan counts the guard, updates, and generated name, but no node for the action record itself. The build appends one ActionDecl per instance at lower.rs:1914-1918. The relational path explicitly includes this per-action unit through successor_work at lower.rs:1308-1312, and per_work also includes it at lower.rs:1833-1837, so omitting it only from per_size makes Limits.nodes and Usage.nodes under-report generated output by up to MAX_ACTIONS (4,096 records). Add one node per non-relational instance to the plan and consume that prepaid node when the action is appended. Add an exact-limit schema regression that fails when the per-instance action record is removed from the charge.

data.reason: One MEDIUM output-budget blocker remains: expanded non-relational action records are not counted in per_size (th created at lower.rs:1822-1826).

data.body: [RESOLVED][MEDIUM] Re-review at 2dd38ab93030871a9592e65c400e38ddbbcdd135 verifies the repair. crates/continuum-cml/src/lower.rs:1873-1906 charges each plain ActionDecl record and owned name. crates/continuum-cml/src/lower.rs:1939 precharges all instances before construction. crates/continuum-cml/src/lower.rs:1976-1984 burns and consumes the prepaid record before append. crates/continuum-cml/tests/resource_bounds.rs:2334-2361 covers output growth and exact node limits.

data.reason: Verified at target 2dd38ab93030871a9592e65c400e38ddbbcdd135. ActionDecl record and owned-name accounting now matches construction, with aggregate precharge and exact-boundary tests.

[LGTM][RISK:HIGH] Whole persisted range be6528fd6e96726e7167d038f672fdb42397d976..2dd38ab93030871a9592e65c400e38ddbbcdd135 reviewed. No unresolved security finding.

Failure modes: Wrong quantifier lowering could hide or add overflow, change strict evaluation, collide action identities, or exceed resource budgets. The target fails closed and accounts for these paths in crates/continuum-cml/src/lower.rs:1388-1513 and 1873-1984.
Edge cases: Reviewed empty domains, empty sets, false guards, nested and repeated binders, configured-set caps, escaped sort elements, action-schema products, relational products, and exact limits.
Rollback: Revert the reviewed range and retain the prior typed refusals if a regression appears.
Monitoring: Track cml.lower.guarded_overflow, output_too_large, work_limit_exceeded, and differential or exact-boundary regressions.
Validation: Inspected production paths and tests in crates/continuum-cml/tests/quantifiers.rs and crates/continuum-cml/tests/resource_bounds.rs:1660-2475. This read-only review did not execute tests.

Risk:critical human approval remains required. This LGTM is only the static Seal verdict.
